Subject: Request: mapping of VM controls to SIG/CAIQ + timelines

Hi Lauren,

We're preparing Acme's SIG and CAIQ review and the reviewers have asked for a concise mapping that ties your vulnerability management controls to our risk-tiers (Critical / High / Medium / Low). In particular, they want:

- The scan cadence (authenticated internal, external, container/image scans) and evidence (samples or reports).
- The SLA you apply for remediation by severity and what constitutes an "exception" (3rd-party deps, external hosted services).
- A signed attestation we can include in our SIG packet that confirms those SLAs and the cadence for the last 12 months.

Can you send: (a) a single spreadsheet that maps SIG/CAIQ control IDs to your VM control, and (b) a short SLA statement or attestation PDF? If possible, we need this by Tue 13 Apr to keep our compliance window.

Thanks — please loop in your security leads if helpful.

Best,
Jamie

Jamie — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the mapping and an attestation. See the materials attached to this message (stubs listed below) and a short summary here.

Quick summary of what we are sending:
- VulnMgmt_RiskTier_Map.xlsx: single-sheet mapping linking SIG/CAIQ control IDs (VM-xxxx) to Redwood processes, owners, and artifacts.
- Scan_Cadence_2027Q2.pdf: the schedule and sample report excerpts (authenticated internal weekly scans, external authenticated weekly, container image scans daily at build time; quarterly external penetration test).
- CVE_Remediation_SLA.docx: our remediation SLAs by risk tier and how exceptions are handled.

Key points from the SLA (high level):
- Critical: triage within 2 business hours, mitigation or compensating control in place within 72 hours unless explicit exception approved by security council.
- High: triage within 8 business hours, remediation target 7 days.
- Medium: remediation target 30 days.
- Low: remediation tracked on regular backlog, target 90 days.

Exceptions policy (short):
- Third-party/managed dependencies where a vendor patch is required: we log the dependency, assign a mitigation (WAF rule/config, network segmentation), and set a monitored exception; vendor remediation timeline is tracked; we escalate externally when vendor ETA exceeds agreed threshold.
- External-hosted partner services: we maintain a documented risk acceptance with the partner; if a critical CVE affects a partner we classify it as a cross-account incident and open a joint action plan.

Notes about evidence scope: the spreadsheet maps to SIG and CAIQ control families and includes sample report IDs (Drive links) that show the last three months of scans. For SOC 2 in-scope evidence, our SOC 2 report (redacted) is linked in the Drive folder.

Next steps: Markus (security lead) and Soojin (compliance) are cc'd and will provide the signed attestation PDF once legal signs off on the wording. We aim to deliver the signed PDF by Mon 12 Apr. If that timing doesn't work for you let us know.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Trust & Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Jamie / Lauren — adding a few implementation details to clarify evidence you'll see in the spreadsheet and Drive: 

- Scans and cadence:
  * Auth internal VM agent scans: weekly, authenticated, stored with report IDs VM-INT-YYYYMM and included as sample excerpts in the PDF.
  * External authenticated scans: weekly (scan vendor: ObservantSec), report IDs VM-EXT-YYYYMM.
  * Container image scanning: performed on every build in CI/CD (daily aggregate report).
  * Quarterly penetration test: vendor summary (redacted findings) is in the Drive folder.

- SLA enforcement & tracking:
  * All high/critical findings create a Jira ticket with prefix SEC-VM (e.g., SEC-VM-231). Tickets include severity, owner, target remediation date.
  * We have an automated playbook that assigns critical findings to the on-call responder and notifies execs if not mitigated in 48 hours.

- Evidence for SIG/CAIQ mapping: spreadsheet columns include control id, control text, evidence artifact type, artifact id (Drive link), and owner. The mapping is intentionally minimal — reviewers usually prefer links to the artifacts.

I'll add a short attestation paragraph to the CVE_Remediation_SLA.docx and coordinate with Legal for signature. If Acme needs the attestation to reference a specific SIG control id, call it out and we'll include it verbatim.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
